## 2. Summary & Long-Form Technical Bio

Sahil Tomar (dev-S-t) is an AI Solutions Engineer specializing in real-time Voice AI infrastructure, agentic workflow orchestration, photorealistic AI video avatars, and high-throughput Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platforms.

Key technical milestones:
- **Production Voice AI Infrastructure (VOAG):** Engineered an enterprise Voice AI SaaS platform processing over 1,000 production calls daily live inside the Mr. LADs application with sub-200ms p95 latency. Built low-latency streaming pipelines connecting WebRTC/SIP telephony with STT/LLM/TTS services (Gemini Realtime, Sarvam, Ultravox).
- **UAE LAN Telephony Bridging:** Deployed a specialized UAE telephony bridge inside a client's private Virtual Machine: SIM card into modem into SIP gateway into self-hosted LiveKit on local LAN behind strict NAT gateways.
- **Hireups AI Avatar Interviewer:** Delivered a real-time photorealistic video avatar interviewer product for MGS Technology (via Quantashift Consultancy Services) across 3 GCP production environments (GCP VM, Cloud Run persistent WebRTC, client private server with ZeroSSL). Features Gemini Realtime audio-native model and Groq/Ultravox fallback routing.
- **WhatsApp B2B Group Dispatch Automation:** Built an automated B2B group dispatch system for a Dubai luxury ground transport company using `whatsmeow` (Go) and Google ADK multi-agent orchestration, reducing turnaround from ~30 minutes to under 1 minute with zero recurring API fees. Extended to an independent musician community routing gateway.
- **MAGe Media Generation Engine:** Designed a multi-agent ad and video generation engine (Google Veo, Playwright brand crawler, Cartesia voice, Subreddit trend scanner, session `contextvars` cost accounting).
- **RAG Architecture & Isolation:** Architected multi-tenant RAG pipelines (AnyAssist) utilizing logical vector namespace isolation and LiteLLM gateway routing, plus Privacy-First On-Prem RAG over Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol.

## 5. Major Engineering Case Studies

### Case Study 1: Data That Can't Leave the Building
- **Problem:** Legal/compliance clients refusing cloud RAG document uploads.
- **Architecture:** Inverted RAG topology over Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol. Reasoning agents deploy locally on client network with hybrid dense vector + keyword search.

### Case Study 2: Multi-Tenant AI Without Cross-Contamination
- **Problem:** Serving multiple clients safely on shared RAG infrastructure.
- **Architecture:** Agent-per-tenant model on Google ADK, logical vector namespace isolation, LiteLLM gateway for cross-provider routing and per-tenant cost attribution.

### Case Study 3: 30 Minutes to Under a Minute — Automating a Manual Dispatch Desk
- **Problem:** Dubai luxury transport company manual B2B WhatsApp group bookings (~30 min turnaround).
- **Architecture:** `whatsmeow` Go connection layer + Python/ADK multi-agents (Orchestrator, Booking Agent with Google Maps and backend tools, Support Agent) + Cloud Run Flight Data service.

### Case Study 4: Filtering Signal From a Thousand Messages a Day
- **Problem:** Musician buried in 1,000+ daily community messages.
- **Architecture:** Extended WhatsApp gateway with group monitoring service forwarding actionable messages to private admin group + fan-out forwarding service.

### Case Study 5: Unblocking a Real-Time Avatar Product After Months Stuck
- **Problem:** MGS/Quantashift internal team stuck getting LiveKit video working for avatar interviewer.
- **Architecture:** Self-hosted LiveKit on GCP driving photorealistic avatar via Gemini Realtime (English & Arabic) across 3 environments (GCP VM, Cloud Run, ZeroSSL private server) with Groq/Ultravox fallback.

### Case Study 6: One Voice Platform, Two Opposite Conversational Goals
- **Problem:** Higher-ed unhurried follow-up vs. real estate persistent cold-calling under sub-200ms latency.
- **Architecture:** VOAG platform on DigitalOcean + UAE LAN SIP modem, regional low-latency workers + Cloud Run auto-scale workers, multi-provider routing (Gemini/Sarvam/Ultravox), fire-and-forget Google File Search RAG.

### Case Study 7: Consistent Brand Content Without a Social Media Manager
- **Problem:** SMB post uncertainty and slow creative execution.
- **Architecture:** MAGe engine: Playwright brand crawler + vision model brand profile, multi-agent pipeline (Veo + Cartesia + FFmpeg frame anchoring), Subreddit sentiment scanner, session `contextvars` cost accounting.

## 6. Major Production Projects

1. **Multi-Tenant RAG Platform (AnyAssist):** Self-service document chat, Google ADK agents, LiteLLM cost/routing gateway, logical vector namespace isolation.
2. **Privacy-First On-Prem RAG (A2A Protocol):** Inverted RAG topology over A2A protocol for local compliance.
3. **WhatsApp Dispatch Automation:** B2B group dispatch for Dubai luxury transport client (`whatsmeow` Go + Google ADK) plus musician community vertical.
4. **VOAG Enterprise Voice AI SaaS:** 1,000+ daily calls in Mr. LADs app, sub-200ms latency, UAE LAN SIP modem architecture, fire-and-forget RAG.
5. **Hireups Real-Time AI Avatar Interviewer:** Photorealistic video avatar interviewer on Gemini Realtime & LiveKit GCP for MGS via Quantashift.
6. **MAGe Media Generation Engine:** Multi-agent creative ad pipeline (Google Veo, Playwright brand crawler, Cartesia, Subreddit trend scanner, session `contextvars` cost accounting).
7. **UniBias Live Attention Tracker:** Browser-side computer vision attention analytics.
8. **Blood Bank Demand-Forecasting System:** IEEE-published SARIMA/XGBoost dynamic micro-expiry simulation.

## 7. Scholarly Publication

- **Title:** *A Demand-Driven Software Approach with Dynamic Micro-Expiry and Just-in-Time Processing to Reduce Platelet Wastage in Blood Banks*
- **Publisher / Venue:** IEEE
- **IEEE Document Link:** https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11584332
- **Author Contribution (Sahil Tomar):** Co-author responsible for ideation, problem formulation, SARIMA/XGBoost model development, and simulation software execution.
- **Validated Results:** Reduced simulated platelet wastage from 11.2% to 2.5% (~78% relative reduction) with 99.1% supply fulfillment (p < 1.22×10⁻¹²).
